title: Lean Negative Inventory

canonical_node.axiom: Every positive claim in the Faith Thru Physics Lean architecture must be paired with a formal negative counterpart: a collapse condition, an insufficiency condition, and at least one adversarial false-positive rejection.
definitions: Negative theorem: a formal statement that asserts the invalidity, insufficiency, or collapse of a proposed positive claim under specified conditions.
Collapse condition: a condition under which the master equation or a key component becomes zero, rendering the overall coherence invalid.
Insufficiency condition: a condition where a single factor or local positivity is not enough to guarantee global coherence or validity.
False-positive rejection: a formal proof that a proposed isomorphism, mapping, or interpretation is invalid because it fails to preserve required structure or signatures.
COMPILED_NOW: negative theorems already present in the active Lean repository and part of the successful package.
WORKBOOK_TARGET: negative chains implied by the workbook and addendum docs, not necessarily formalized in the root package.
MISSING_TARGET: negative families that should exist but are not yet clearly formalized.
derivation: The master equation is a product of factors; any single zero factor collapses the product to zero (proved by theorems like Q_zero_collapses_chi).
Nonzero factors are not sufficient to rescue global coherence; necessity is proven, not sufficiency (e.g., Q_nonzero_not_sufficient_for_positive_chi).
Coupling states are irreversible; C0_ne_C1 and C1_ne_C0 prevent relabeling objections.
Mapping layer is not arbitrary; signature layer rejects swaps like grace_swapped_with_faith_invalid.
Fracture and fall are distinguished from generic gaps or separation; random_gap_is_not_structured_scar and pre_fall_is_not_fall.
Counterfeit coherence is rejected; no_mere_order_as_full_coherence and related theorems block fake wins.
Stage reversal is impossible; no_stage_step_back_to_pre_from_localization and others enforce one-way transitions.
Law bypasses force zero; law3_command_bypass_forces_E_zero and others prove each bypass is a collapse condition.
Isomorphism claims are guarded; no_rich_iso_to_natural_coin and others reject false positives.
The workbook targets additional negative chains (Maxwell/Trinity, justice/mercy, resurrection, memory, hit-rate) that must be made explicit.
Missing targets include full per-factor insufficiency, dependency-lattice rejection, sign/conversion rejection, resurrection false-positive family, and full isomorphism-chain inventory.
canonical_node.action: Maintain and extend the negative inventory so that every positive claim in the architecture is accompanied by formal negative theorems: collapse conditions, insufficiency conditions, and false-positive rejections. Prioritize formalizing WORKBOOK_TARGET and MISSING_TARGET families.
boundary: This document does not itself contain formal proofs; it is an inventory of existing and needed negative theorems.
It does not assert that all listed negative theorems are currently formalized; statuses are explicitly marked.
It does not upgrade theological claims into physical proofs; it only records the negative side of the Lean program.
It does not claim completeness; it explicitly lists missing targets.
test: For each positive claim in the architecture, verify that there exists at least one formal negative theorem addressing collapse, insufficiency, and false-positive rejection.
Check that all COMPILED_NOW theorems are present in the active Lean repository and compile successfully.
Check that WORKBOOK_TARGET chains are either formalized or explicitly tracked as pending.
Check that MISSING_TARGET families are either formalized or listed as open work items.
Review that no positive claim is made without a corresponding negative counterpart in the inventory.

dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides a centralized, reviewable inventory of all negative theorems and negative theorem families in the Lean program, distinguishing compiled, workbook-target, and missing targets, enabling systematic completion of the negative architecture.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the existing compiled negative theorems and their status as COMPILED_NOW, ensuring they remain visible and load-bearing.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: If this inventory is removed, the negative side of the architecture becomes fragmented and unverifiable; missing negative families may be overlooked, leading to overclaiming and unguarded positive claims.

classification.claim_class: Inventory of negative theorems and targets
classification.recommended_atom_action: Track as a living inventory; formalize missing targets; use as a checklist for negative coverage.

overstatement_risks: May imply that all listed negative theorems are formally proven when some are only workbook targets or missing.
May overstate the completeness of the negative architecture.
May conflate theological necessity with mathematical proof.
kill_conditions: If a listed COMPILED_NOW theorem is not actually present in the Lean repo, the inventory's credibility collapses.
If the inventory is used to claim that the architecture is locked down without formalizing missing targets, it becomes misleading.
If negative theorems are misinterpreted as positive proofs of theological claims.
risk.lean_target: Formalize all WORKBOOK_TARGET and MISSING_TARGET negative families in Lean, ensuring every positive chain has collapse, insufficiency, and false-positive rejection.

plain_summary: This document is a catalog of negative theorems and negative theorem families in the Faith Thru Physics Lean program. It lists already-compiled negative theorems (e.g., zero-factor collapse, coupling irreversibility, mapping invalidation, fracture/fall distinctions, counterfeit coherence, stage reversal, law bypasses, isomorphism guards), workbook-target chains (Maxwell/Trinity, justice/mercy, resurrection, memory, hit-rate), and missing targets (per-factor insufficiency, dependency-lattice, sign/conversion, resurrection false-positives, isomorphism-chain inventory). It serves as a reviewable checklist to ensure every positive claim has a corresponding negative counterpart, but it does not itself contain formal proofs.
